| [QUESTION-378](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-378.md) | Under what conditions does coupling two locally rigid organizational subsystems create new adaptive degrees of freedom at their interface? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 5. The readings answer the mechanical version only under conditions, and the question is asked with them. A flexible interface between rigid kirigami needs the two sides in topologically distinct phases, and the opposite pairing or orientation gives a stressed line instead (Chen et al.; Kane and Lubensky). A link joining two components of a linkage removes three rigid-body freedoms and adds one internal one (Chen, Choi and Mahadevan). Decoupled units in series add nothing new (Jules et al.). So coupling rigid parts does not in general create freedom. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |

| [QUESTION-429](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-429.md) | Does an independent re-analysis of Banerjee, Hanna, Kreindler and Olken's harmonized micro-data, or a further pooled analysis of randomized evaluations of government cash transfer programmes, find no systematic effect of the transfers on whether adults work or on their weekly hours, with moderate reductions excluded for men? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-1471](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1471.md), moved here when the twenty-eighth status review promoted it under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md): [THEORY-1471](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1471.md) reports what the authors' pooled re-analysis of seven trials measured; whether an independent analysis agrees is this question. | Open |
| [QUESTION-430](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-430.md) | Does an independent study using randomly sized windfalls, in another lottery, state or period, find that large winners' lower rate of bankruptcy in the first two years or so after winning is offset by a higher rate later, leaving no detectable difference over about five years, and that large winners who file have net assets and unsecured debt like small winners who file? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-1490](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1490.md), moved here when the twenty-eighth status review promoted it under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md). It read: 'An independent study using randomly sized windfalls, in another lottery, state or period, finds that large winners' lower rate of bankruptcy in the first two years or so after winning is offset by a higher rate later, leaving no detectable difference over about five years, and that large winners who file have net assets and unsecured debt like small winners who file; or the published Review of Economics and Statistics version, once read, reports the same two-year decline, year 3–5 rise, five-year null and balance sheets at filing.' Its version-of-record route was dropped under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §4; the independent-study route is this question. | Open |
| [QUESTION-432](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-432.md) | Do aid-funded projects whose beneficiaries stated the demand, contributed their own resources, received the benefits and shared the decision to continue keep their benefits after donor support ends more often than projects funded and controlled by the donor, and does a recipient's own spending on maintaining donor-funded assets fall as its expectation of donor repair rises? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-1480](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1480.md), moved here when the twenty-ninth status review promoted [THEORY-1480](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1480.md) as a report of what Ostrom, Gibson, Shivakumar and Andersson (2002) hold. The authors assert both parts and test neither; whether aid bears them out is this question. | Open |
| [QUESTION-436](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-436.md) | Does an independent threshold-regression test of unique against multiple equilibria, on the Japanese bombing data or another large temporary shock to cities, find a preferred multiple-equilibria model whose intercepts satisfy the ordering that larger negative shocks lead to lower equilibria? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-1503](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1503.md), moved here when the twenty-ninth status review narrowed and promoted it under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md). It read: 'The Journal of Regional Science version of record (48(1), 2008) read and found to report, as the working paper does, that the Schwarz criterion prefers a unique equilibrium for aggregate city manufacturing and for city-industry output, and that the best-fitting multiple-equilibria models for population and industries violate the intercept-ordering criterion; or an independent threshold test on the same Japanese data that finds the same. Refuted if a corrected or re-run test admits a multiple-equilibria model that satisfies the ordering criterion and is preferred. Whether temporary interventions could select equilibria is the authors' policy reading, not asserted here.' Its version-of-record route was dropped under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §4, since no discrepancy between versions is named; the independent test, with its refutation clause, is this question. | Open |
